sentences.text: Marasuchus is an early genus of dinosauriform archosaur and a close relative of dinosaurs.
Its body featured long, slender limbs where the hindlimbs were about twice the length of the forelimbs, and the entire forelimb was roughly half the size of the hindlimb.
The animal possessed a relatively long neck with an S-shaped curve and a very long, thin tail that was deeper at the base.
Although several specimens show most of the skeleton, skull material is limited and the hand is entirely unknown.
The braincase was tall and typical for early archosaurs but shared some similarities with early dinosaur braincases.
Most of the unique traits that define Marasuchus are found in its vertebrae.
A long, curved neck was created by elongated neck vertebrae with offset ends, similar to other bird-lineage archosaurs.
The upper blade of the hip, the ilium, was similar in general shape to that of Herrerasaurus.
A ridge of bone called the trochanteric shelf branched from the anterior trochanter and wrapped around the femur shaft.
Marasuchus is one of the most completely known avemetatarsalians, providing key insights into the early evolution of dinosaur-like traits.
The species Marasuchus lilloensis was originally named Lagosuchus lilloensis in 1972, but the type species of the genus Marasuchus is Marasuchus illoensis, described by Sereno and Arcucci in 1994.
Marasuchus fossils were named after specimens stored at the PVL museum in San Miguel de Tucuman.
The first known remains were found during a 1964-1965 paleontological expedition, which Alfred Romer described in a series of papers.
The holotype specimen PVL 3871 was collected by Jose Bonaparte in 1969.
Lagosuchus lilloensis, described by Romer in 1972, is a synonym of Marasuchus, having been originally described as a second species of Lagosuchus, named L. lilloensis.

In a 1994 restudy, Sereno and Arcucci concluded that the original Lagosuchus type specimen was too poorly preserved to allow adding additional specimens to that genus, noting that the L. lilloensis specimen had different limb proportions compared to the type species.
Its body proportions suggest Marasuchus was probably bipedal, walking on its hindlimbs.
Marasuchus was a small predator only 40 centimeters long.
Marasuchus belonged to Avemetatarsalia, the archosaur branch closer to birds and dinosaurs than to crocodilians.
It was classified as a dinosauriform, placing it closer to dinosaurs than to lagerpetids.
Marasuchus lived in the Late Triassic (early Carnian stage) in what is now La Rioja Province, Argentina, with fossils coming from the Chañares Formation, dated to 235 to 234 million years ago.

Other sources describe it as an extinct ornithodiran archosaur that lived during the Middle Triassic (Ladinian, about 230 million years ago) in the Chañares Formation in La Rioja, Argentina, or state it lived from 241.464 to 237 million years ago during the Ladinian stage.

It is debated whether Marasuchus is a valid genus or a junior synonym of Lagosuchus. A 2019 study suggested that Marasuchus lilloensis might be a synonym of Lagosuchus talampayensis after re-examining the type specimen, while a 2024 study concluded that Marasuchus and Lagosuchus represent the same animal, with Lagosuchus talampayensis having priority.
